title: お～ / ご～ — polite prefixes on nouns
summary: お and ご are polite prefixes put before a noun to show respect to the listener or to make speech more refined. Native Japanese words (和語) mostly take お, and Sino-Japanese words (漢語) mostly take ご.

patterns.gloss: お + native Japanese noun (お名前, お茶, お元気)
ご + Sino-Japanese noun (ご家族, ご連絡)

body.p: お is usually used with words read in the native Japanese way (名前, 茶, 元気 as お名前, お茶, お元気). ご is usually used with words read in the Chinese-derived way (家族, 連絡 as ご家族, ご連絡).
When it respects another person, the prefix goes on their things or actions: お名前 (your name), ご家族 (your family). Never put it on your own: say 私の名前, not お名前.
Some words almost always carry お even when no honor is meant: お茶, お金, お水, お風呂, お弁当, ご飯. There are exceptions (e.g., お電話 and ご飯), so learn them as set words.

examples.ja: お名前（なまえ）を教（おし）えてください。
examples.note: お respects the other person's name.
お茶 is a fixed polite word.

examples.ja: ご家族（かぞく）はお元気（げんき）ですか。
examples.note: ご + 家族 (Sino-Japanese), お + 元気 (also takes お).

pitfalls: Don't add お/ご to your own things or family. Say 私の家族, not ご家族, for your own.
Not every noun takes a prefix (e.g., 電車, 車). Learn which words are normally used with お/ご.
